# Phase 23: zero-copy tier, selection on the device

Gap table item 5 and note 2. Since [Phase 4](PHASE_4.md) the CPU tier (rung 6) has decoded at about
half rung 5's speed, and [Phase 11](PHASE_11.md) traced that to the host: every selecting layer
brings its top-K block ids back to the CPU, updates a residency table, and launches copies.
Prefetch (rung 7) hid the copies and gained nothing. The gap table named a residency decision made on
the GPU as the honest successor and left it unbuilt. This phase builds one form of it. Questions were
fixed in `configs/phase23.yaml` before any run.

## What was built

- **`pinned.device_view`**: pinned host memory is mapped into the GPU's address space under
  unified addressing. This asks the CUDA runtime for the device-side address of a pinned tensor
  and wraps it as a CUDA tensor, so a kernel that indexes it reads host RAM over PCIe directly
  ("zero-copy"). No transfer is launched. No new dependency: the runtime library ships with torch.
- **`fetch="zerocopy"`** (`TieredLayer.gather_zerocopy`, policy `tiered_zerocopy`): each selecting
  layer ranks blocks on the GPU and gathers the top K straight from the host pool's device view. The
  block ids never reach the host, so there is no sync, no residency table and no slot pool. VRAM
  holds the sink and the current block per layer. Same blocks in the same order as rung 5.
- **The trade**, by design: every step reads every selected block over the link, whether or not it
  was read the step before. Rung 6 moves only misses, but pays host work for every selection.
- Tests: bit-identical logits to rung 5 under both attention kernels, across seals, and with dense
  turn ingestion (Phase 21). Rung 9, prefetch and selection replay refuse the mode, since they need
  residency or host-side ids.

## Question 1: speed

Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, 32,768-token context, 64-token blocks, the speed kernel, an idle machine.
3 independent runs, each 3
repeats of 128 decode tokens; within a repeat every condition decodes from the same prefill, so the
ratios are paired. Decode per token, median across runs (range of the run medians):

| Budget | Rung 5 | Rung 6 (gather, spare 1.0) | Zero-copy tier | Zero-copy / rung 6, paired | Zero-copy / rung 5, paired | Manager host time, rung 6 / zero-copy |
| --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| 50% | 24.4 ms (24.2–24.6) | 30.4 ms (30.2–30.5) | 77.6 ms (75.9–78.4) | 2.55 (0 / 9 pairs faster) | 3.13 | 9.7 ms / 6.8 ms |
| 25% | 25.5 ms (25.2–28.9) | 52.4 ms (52.4–53.5) | 44.2 ms (43.9–45.3) | 0.85 (9 / 9 pairs faster) | 1.72 | 20.7 ms / 6.1 ms |
| 12.5% | 26.0 ms (25.1–26.7) | 50.6 ms (50.6–52.5) | 30.1 ms (29.0–30.3) | 0.60 (9 / 9 pairs faster) | 1.15 | 20.5 ms / 5.8 ms |
| 6.25% | 29.4 ms (25.9–29.7) | 53.5 ms (52.7–54.6) | 26.8 ms (25.8–29.2) | 0.55 (9 / 9 pairs faster) | 0.99 | 21.2 ms / 6.9 ms |

The full cache decodes at 18.8 ms per token in the same runs.

- **At 25% and below, the zero-copy tier is faster than rung 6 in every paired repeat**, by
  1.18× at 25%,
  1.67× at 12.5% and
  1.82× at 6.25%. At 6.25% it runs at rung 5's speed
  (ratio 0.99), so the tier's
  host overhead is gone there. The manager's host time per token drops to rung 5's level, because the
  host no longer touches the selection.
- **At 50% it is 0.39× rung 6's speed, so much slower.**
  Every step reads half the context's KV over PCIe. Rung 6 at 50% with one spare slot per selected
  block holds nearly every block in VRAM (see question 2), so it moves almost nothing. The crossover
  lies between 25% and 50% on this machine; it was not located more finely.
- So the speed the device-side decision recovers depends on the budget: all of it at 6.25%, most of it at 12.5%, less at 25%, and
  none at 50%. The zero-copy tier's cost grows with K; rung 6's is host work that does not.

## Question 2: memory

Resident KV (VRAM) per condition, from the same runs:

| Budget | Rung 5 | Rung 6 | Zero-copy tier |
| --: | --: | --: | --: |
| 50% | 1,028 MiB | 1,103 MiB | 146 MiB |
| 25% | 1,028 MiB | 651 MiB | 146 MiB |
| 12.5% | 1,028 MiB | 427 MiB | 146 MiB |
| 6.25% | 1,028 MiB | 315 MiB | 146 MiB |

- The zero-copy tier holds the same amount at every budget: the two dense layers' KV plus a sink and
  a current block per selecting layer. Rung 6 holds slots for its selection and spares, staging
  buffers, and the same dense layers. Rung 5 holds the whole cache, as does the full cache
  (1028 MiB).

## Question 3: validity at scale

The ladder's 45 NIAH prompts and 2 teacher-forced windows at 32K, quality kernel, rung 5 and the
zero-copy tier in one process:

| Budget | NIAH answers equal to rung 5's | Teacher-forced KL equal to rung 5's |
| --: | --: | --: |
| 12.5% | 45 / 45 | 2 / 2 |
| 6.25% | 45 / 45 | 2 / 2 |

**The zero-copy tier gives rung 5's answer on 90 of 90 prompts and its teacher-forced KL on 4 of 4 windows**, at both budgets. It reads the same bytes in the same order, as the unit tests said.

## What this phase does not show

- One model and one context. The zero-copy cost is K blocks per layer per step, so a longer context
  at the same budget fraction reads proportionally more; at 130K and 6.25% that is as many bytes as
  32K at 25%. Not measured.
- The PCIe link here is the laptop's. On a faster link the crossover moves up; on a slower one, down.
- No hybrid was built (keep hot blocks in VRAM, read the rest in place). It would need a
  residency decision on the device that never brings sizes back to the host, which plain PyTorch
  cannot express without a sync; it was left out rather than half built.
